description: Minimum machine-readable constitution for the documentation authority migration: exactly the plan §6.3 rules. It encodes docs/doc-governance.md for the migration; it is not a second prose governance and not the future docs/doc-types.yaml engine manifest.

reuses.what: Document types, placement map, authority matrix and conflict rules, metadata baseline, subcomponent shape, writing method and typed relationships. The constitution restates only the machine-checkable part and links back.
authorityStatus values (legacy-current, candidate, promoted, non-authority), fileClass values and the rule that the switchboard, not a path or date, decides authority during migration.
One-owner discipline, candidate marker in the Design status field, legacy-root ratchet and its exception ledger.

The invariant activeDoc(topicId, role) <= 1 is reused as the singleton cardinality rule; the registry lifecycle names (reserved, provisional, active, superseded, retired) are reused when document lifecycle is modeled later (deferred). No second registry or event store is introduced.
Only the plan §6.3 items are taken: placement, cardinality, required metadata, authority conflict handling, promotion and retirement gates. Everything else is listed under deferredToEngine.

placementRules.rule: Maintained platform authority lives under docs/platform/**: platform-wide documents directly under docs/platform/, area documents under docs/platform/<area>/.
No new maintained prose under the legacy roots docs/specs/** and docs/architect/**; the legacy-docs ratchet enforces it.
Each document kind may live only at one of its listed placement patterns.
A file's class is decided by its claims and consumers, never by its physical location alone (plan §2.3).

domains/, .agents/skills/, plugins/fgOS/skills/ and plans/ stay outside the docs/platform topology. They follow the document taxonomy but are shipped or working surfaces, not moved by the cutover (plan §3 item 11).

requiredMetadata.appliesTo: Every maintained canonical document and every candidate document under docs/platform/**.
requiredMetadata.headerForm: A fenced txt block directly under the H1 with plain `Field: value` lines.

candidateMarker.source: authorityStatus of the area or route in the transitional switchboard (docs/transitional-switchboard.md and transitional-switchboard.json)
candidateMarker.rule: A document is a candidate or promoted according to the switchboard, never according to the text of its Design status field. Draft, Proposed and Candidate in Design status are descriptive only; promoted portals say Draft today.

structure: exactly one H1, and it is the document title
every section starts at H2; maintained canonical documents use numbered headings
relationships listed in the Related field are also markdown links in the body
a document that lists related paths links them with relative markdown links
requiredMetadata.evidence: The six promotedCore fields are present in all 72 headered documents under docs/platform/** and in all three promoted area portals; the other six fields are present in 13 of them (measured by script on the plan branch, 2026-10-06).

rules: A generated document names its source of truth and generator and states Do not edit: true.
Generated output never outranks its source and is never edited by hand.
A generated projection must be reproducible and carry its freshness information.
History and evidence establish no current claim and are not default reading authority.
History is kept only with an explicit relationship from a canonical document or an alias, and with a recorded reason.
Evidence payloads may be relocated before the cutover only after their consumers are inventoried and their digests verified.

unclassified.rule: A file with no switchboard route stays unknown-blocking until an area assigns its class; it blocks the cutover.

authorityConflict.principle: A conflict is a documentation defect. Surface and reconcile it; no agent silently chooses a winner.

precedence.rule: A current spec outranks stale architecture wording about present behavior.
A newer approved decision supersedes an older one.
Generated output never outranks its source.

procedure: Detect: duplicate-content groups, semantic-conflict groups, two claim rows with different owners, or a reader-reported contradiction.
Record: keep every conflicting claim row with disposition unknown-blocking and reviewStatus blocking, and relate the rows to each other.
Classify the conflict: identical duplicate, stale versus current, contradictory decision, or contract versus guide.
Resolve mechanically only when one precedence rule above applies; otherwise record an owner decision with its rationale.
Encode the outcome in dispositions so exactly one canonical owner remains.
Close the conflict only when no claim has two owners and the surviving rows are reviewed.

promotionGate.definition: A candidate document or claim becomes canonical. Promotion is atomic for the whole platform-documentation system (plan §3 item 5); until the cutover every target stays a candidate.

checks.rule: Every retained claim row has exactly one targetOwner and no unknown-blocking row remains for the promoted sources.
No unreviewed edit or new maintained file under the legacy roots.
The document meets requiredMetadata and its placement pattern.
Every relative link and Related path resolves.
Every claim row of the document has reviewStatus reviewed.
The intent ledger is updated when the document narrows a vision, and the component-boundary check is recorded.

retirementGate.definition: A legacy source may be deleted or redirected only when all checks pass, at the atomic cutover.

checks.rule: The file has one non-blocking file-level disposition.
No claim row of the file is unknown-blocking or unreviewed.
Every entry of the dropped-claims register has a reviewed disposition.
Immutable historical references to the file resolve through the alias table.
Every consumer edge is rewritten or proven non-authority.
Relocated evidence payloads match their recorded digests.

enforcedBy.deliverable: evidence relocation policy and consumer proof

checks.rule: The cutover runs under the migration documentation-cutover lease.
Every claim identity of the previous ledger and identity registry is present in the current row set, or has a recorded removal with rationale and disposition.
Rows that share a semanticClaimId name one distinct targetOwner.
The ledger validator runs in a cutover mode: every retained claim has an owner, an anchor, a classified kind and review status reviewed, and vocabulary usage drift is fatal.

amendmentRule: The constitution is frozen at major version 1 for the meaning of every existing rule. Additions (a document kind, a placement, a gate check) are made by recorded exception with evidence and keep the pinned vocabulary major version; a change to an existing rule needs a new major version and an owner decision.

areaNameRules.definition: Directory names directly under docs/platform/ that hold platform-wide collections; they are never area names.

placementPrecedence: Each path belongs to exactly one document kind. A header marker of a kind wins; otherwise the most specific matching pattern wins (fewest ** segments, then fewest placeholders). Equally specific patterns of different kinds are an error. <placeholder> matches one path segment (inside a segment it matches the rest of the name); ** matches one or more segments.

placementExceptions.reason: Migration-time authoring rules; temporary and retired with the cutover, so it gets no permanent kind.
